# THE CARDS

*The deck as it will be held: twenty-seven faces composed from the sealed knot
map. A working whose open question is not whether it is good but whether the
room needs it.*

## I · WHAT IT IS

Every card, composed as an object a hand could hold. The mandala face over its
profile; the written code at the foot in the card's own metal and the name in
white, their sizes standing four to three, the perfect fourth; the two
diagonals closing the face, a card's own number and its answer's number in
their metals across one, the signed number and its negation, neutral, across
the other.

Nothing on the face is drawn by hand. Every figure derives from the canon's
sealed knot map, so the faces cannot drift from the deck they depict.

## II · WHAT IT TEACHES THAT THE OTHERS DO NOT

Turned upside down, a card's corners read as its answer's corners: an inverted
card announces another card, and is never itself reversed. That is the
involution made physical, and it is a property of the object rather than of any
text about the object. It is the thing this surface knows best.

## III · THE OPEN QUESTION

The architect's own words: it goes somewhere, but there is already a lot of
material on the cards.

That is the difficulty exactly, and it is not a criticism of the surface. The
Book of Luminara teaches the faces. The Illustrated Guide draws them. The
Wayfinder's own Guide shows each card with its form, its number, its answer
across the mirror and its depth, and now carries the census of the whole deck
at its foot. A fourth surface teaching the faces has to earn the fourth
telling.

The strongest case for it is section II: this is the only place the deck exists
as a held object rather than a read one, and the corner-reading is legible
nowhere else. The strongest case against is that the same knowledge now reaches
a person three other ways, and a system is easier to hold when each thing lives
in one place.

## IV · WHAT IT ASKS

Whether the deck needs a room for the object as distinct from the reading. If
it does, this is that room and it is largely built. If it does not, what is
worth keeping is the corner-reading, which could be carried into the Guide the
way the census was, and the surface struck.

## V · WHERE IT STANDS

## VI · PROVENANCE

*Built as prototype faces for the architect's eye during the redesign arc, from
the canon's sealed map, and left unlinked. This chart entered the room on 19
July 2026, when the workings were given a shelf. The question in section III is
the architect's own, recorded as he put it; the weighing is this chart's, and it
argues both sides because the decision is his. Nothing here predicts, and
nothing here prescribes.*
